questions.prompt: Match each mixture to the best separation method.
questions.explain: Each method matches a property: boiling point, how far a dye travels, density when spun, immiscible layers, and a solid that sublimes.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of simple distillation of salt water in order.
steps: Heat the salt water in a flask
Water boils and turns into vapour
Vapour passes into the cold condenser
Pure water (distillate) collects in the beaker
questions.explain: Heat → boil → condenser → condense → collect. The salt stays in the flask.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the condenser in distillation?
options: To cool the vapour so it turns back into a liquid
questions.explain: Cold water around the condenser removes heat from the vapour, so it condenses into the distillate.

questions.prompt: In chromatography the solvent moved 10 cm and a red dye moved 4.5 cm. What is the Rf value of the red dye?
questions.hint: Rf = distance moved by the dye ÷ distance moved by the solvent.

questions.prompt: Why is the starting line in chromatography drawn in PENCIL, not pen?
options: Pencil graphite does not dissolve and run with the solvent
Pen would make the paper wet
questions.explain: Ink from a pen would dissolve and separate too, spoiling the results. Graphite stays put.

questions.prompt: A sweet's colour has Rf 0.75. Allowed food colour A has Rf 0.75 and banned colour B has Rf 0.30 (same solvent). What can you conclude?
options: The sweet contains banned colour B
The sweet's colour matches allowed colour A
questions.explain: Same Rf in the same solvent suggests the same substance, so the colour matches A.

questions.prompt: Alcohol (boils at 78 °C) and water (100 °C) are mixed. Which method separates them best?
questions.explain: They are miscible liquids with different boiling points, so fractional distillation works; alcohol distils off first.

questions.prompt: Which are uses of CENTRIFUGATION? Choose all that apply.
options: Separating blood cells from plasma in a lab
Drying clothes in a washing machine
questions.explain: Spinning throws denser parts outward or down. Salt from sea water uses evaporation; dyes use chromatography.

questions.prompt: Why is crystallisation better than evaporating to dryness when purifying copper sulfate?
options: Impurities stay in the solution, and the crystals are not damaged by overheating
It uses no heat at all
questions.explain: Evaporating to dryness leaves impurities in the solid and can decompose it. Crystallisation gives pure, well-formed crystals.

questions.text: Liquids like oil and water that do not mix are called ___ liquids and can be separated with a separating ___ .
questions.explain: Immiscible liquids form layers; a separating funnel drains the bottom layer.

questions.prompt: Give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of using distillation (or desalination) to make drinking water for a big city.
questions.modelAnswer: Advantage: it can turn sea water (an almost unlimited supply) into pure drinking water, which helps coastal cities during droughts. Disadvantage: it uses a lot of energy, which is expensive and may cause pollution, and the very salty waste water can harm sea life.
rubric: I gave a clear advantage (e.g. unlimited sea water, pure water)
I gave a clear disadvantage (e.g. energy cost, pollution, salty waste)
I explained WHY it matters for people or the environment
questions.explain: Criterion D asks you to weigh the benefits and costs of science in society.
